Subject: Request: proof points + localisation checklist for Kestrel POC

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — KestrelHealth is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. Our security team has asked for a short set of deliverables we need to close the POC: a cross-border safeguards proof pack, a DPA annex template, and confirmation of data residency/localisation options for our US/EU patient data.

Concretely, can you provide the following by COB Monday?
- Short evidence pack listing technical controls (encryption, KMS, HSM, key separation).
- DPF/SCC fallback approach for EU->US processing and any Redwood-prescribed mitigations.
- A simple network diagram showing control plane/data paths for Hosted vs. Dedicated vs. Private.
- DPA Annex template and guidance on the fields customers need to populate.

I've attached our questionnaire (kestrel-questionnaire.xlsx) so you can point to specific rows. If you prefer, we can do a 30-min alignment call early next week.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Director, Cloud Security
KestrelHealth

Subject: Re: Request: proof points + localisation checklist for Kestrel POC

Hi Alice — great to hear. Attaching a compact proof pack and a DPA annex template to address the rows in your spreadsheet. Quick summary below; see attachments for formal exhibits.

Attachments included: redwood-crossborder-proofpoints.pdf, redwood-dpa-annex-template.docx

High-level answers (short):
- Encryption: All customer data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3). Customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS with separate encryption keys per customer.
- Key management: HSM-backed keys (AWS CloudHSM equivalent) for Dedicated and Private deployments; bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via supported KMS providers available.
- Cross-border / DPF: For EU-origin data we support (1) hosting in EU-only regions, (2) routing to EU-dedicated capacity, or (3) EU->US with SCCs + supplemental technical safeguards (pseudonymization, end-to-end TLS, strict access controls). The attached proof pack lists our PCC/DPF mappings and audit artifacts.
- Data residency: Hosted customers can pin model inference to region (EU/US/APAC) for inference and optional log retention locality. Dedicated and Private offer full control over physical location.
- Evidence: We included pointers to SOC2 report sections, sample network diagram, and a mapping of questionnaire rows to Redwood artifacts.

If it's helpful, Karthik (cc'ed) can provide a short technical note on pseudonymization and KV-cache behavior when serving EU keys. Also happy to schedule a short call Monday to walk these items.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Technical clarifications: pseudonymization, KV-cache, and DPF mitigations

Hi Alice / Ben — adding a few technical details to the packet that often come up in assessments. Attaching a simple network diagram for Hosted vs Dedicated (network-diagram.png).

Key clarifications:
1) Pseudonymization at rest / in memory: We support token-level redaction and field-level pseudonymization at the application layer before tokens are sent to the model. For customers who require additional assurance, we offer a pre-processing shim (library) that strips PHI and stores a reversible token map under customer-managed keys.

2) KV cache behavior: For streaming generation we use per-request session caches. For Dedicated/Private capacity caches do not leave the pinned region; for Hosted we can configure strict KV sharding to regional pools. Cache encryption is enforced and cache keys are isolated per-customer.

3) DPF/SCC approach (practical fallback): Our standard contract offers SCCs for controller-processor relationships. Where customers need additional safeguards for EU->US processing we recommend a layered approach:
  - Contractual: SCCs + DPA Annex with specific processing categories and subprocessors enumerated.
  - Organizational: Access controls, limited personnel for cross-border queues, dedicated audit logs.
  - Technical: Pseudonymization + short TTLs for logs and cached artifacts; encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys where feasible.

4) Audit artifacts: The attached proof pack enumerates log retention screenshots, SOC2 sections, and our change control playbook. For customers requiring more, we can provide transient access to a redacted evidence bundle under NDA.

If you want, we can highlight the particular rows in kestrel-questionnaire.xlsx where these answers map; otherwise we can do a 30-min technical review call Monday morning.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference
